contract: Lists the image names of one Docker, OCI or Helm OCI repository, in the shape of the registry _catalog extension. An image is a folder holding at least one manifest. contract: Returns .npmrc lines that point an npm scope at one npm repository and authenticate the caller to it. The first line is `@<scope>:registry=<registry URL>`, where the registry URL is `<base>/artifactory/api/npm/<repoKey>/`. The credential lines follow, each keyed to that URL without its scheme (`//<host>/artifactory/api/npm/<repoKey>/:`), so npm sends them to this registry only. A caller that sent Basic credentials gets `_password=<base64>` and `username=<user>`, where the base64 is of its encrypted password, the value `GET /api/security/encryptedPassword` returns, or of the token it sent as its password; the password itself is never returned. A caller that sent a token as a Bearer token or in `X-JFrog-Art-Api` gets `_authToken=<token>` with that same token. Any npm repository can be named, local, remote or virtual. Needs an authenticated caller. Errors use the `{"errors":[{"status","message"}]}` envelope. Because this operation owns GET <registry>/auth/<scope>, a package named auth cannot have its version manifests read through the registry; its packument and tarballs are unaffected.

contract: Reads metadata about a file or folder. Without a mode parameter the response is `FileInfo` for a file or `FolderInfo` for a folder. Exactly one of `properties`, `lastModified`, `stats`, `permissions` or `list` selects another view and changes the response shape and media type accordingly. Needs read permission; `list` additionally refuses anonymous callers, `lastModified` needs deploy permission and `permissions` needs admin. Works on local repositories, remote caches and virtual repositories, and on the trash can under the key `auto-trashcan`, whose root holds a folder per repository with deleted items and below it their original paths. There a file's information adds its `trash.*` properties, `properties` shows the item's own properties and `trash.time` (Unix milliseconds), `trash.deletedBy`, `trash.originalRepository`, `trash.originalRepositoryType` and `trash.originalPath`, `stats` shows no downloads, and `permissions` answers 400. A caller other than an admin sees only what was deleted from repositories where it holds deploy or manage permission, in every view, and is refused with 403 at a path where it sees nothing. While the trash can is disabled every view under `auto-trashcan`, its root included, answers 404 to any caller, an admin included; the items it holds are kept and can still be restored, cleaned or emptied.

contract: Streams the content of a file. Resolution follows the repository class: local serves stored content, remote serves the cache or fetches from upstream, virtual walks its members in order. Matrix parameters `;key=value` on the path restrict resolution to items carrying those properties. The version tokens `[RELEASE]`, `[INTEGRATION]` and `SNAPSHOT` resolve to the latest matching version in a repository whose layout defines both `[folderItegRev]` and `[fileItegRev]`; elsewhere the path is looked up as written. Supports `Range` requests with 206 and exposes `X-Checksum-Md5`, `X-Checksum-Sha1` and `X-Checksum-Sha256` headers. Each completed download updates the statistics unless `skipUpdateStats=true`. In a repository with `downloadRedirect` or `cdnRedirect`, a GET of a file at least `download.redirect.min_size` long answers 302 to a signed URL on the CDN in front of the blob store, if it has one, or on the object store itself (`downloadRedirect` only), carrying the file name and media type as response overrides. HEAD and conditional requests are always answered here. A path ending in `.md5`, `.sha1`, `.sha256` or `.sha512` beside a file answers that checksum of the file as plain text: under `client-checksums` the one the client sent, and 404 while it has sent none (every deploy records the SHA-256); under `server-generated-checksums`, for `maven-metadata.xml` and in a remote cache, the computed one.

contract: With grant_type client_credentials (the default) mints a new access token for username, or for the caller when username is omitted. With grant_type refresh_token exchanges refresh_token for a new access token with the same scope and audience. The body may be JSON or form-encoded. A non-admin may only mint identity tokens for themselves (scope applied-permissions/user). Admins may mint any scope that a user already holds; scopes only narrow. A transient user, the subject of a token minted for a name that is no stored user or of an OIDC exchange, mints for itself a token with its own token's scope that resolves to the same transient user. That token expires no later than the caller's own token, and may be refreshable only when the caller's own token is, or the request is refused with 403. A user name and password sent with Basic mint a token only while the token.allow_basic_auth setting is on, which it is not by default; an access or reference token, as Bearer or as the Basic password, always may. The response status is 200 and the body always carries token_id.

contract: Rebuilds the package index of a local npm repository from the tarballs it holds and their properties. Each tarball on its canonical path is read again for its package.json, and its npm.disttag and npm.deprecated properties give the dist-tags and deprecations, latest among them; a package none of whose tarballs carries latest gets it on the version that ranks highest, a release above every pre-release and then the higher SemVer, written as that tarball's npm.disttag=latest. Packuments and version manifests are then served from the rebuilt index. Package metadata is derived from the index, so a reindex rewrites index entries and properties, never files. Tarballs off their canonical path, or without a readable package.json, stay unindexed until the strict-layout conversion moves them. The rebuild is queued on the persistent work queue under the repository's key and runs in the background; the 200, whose text is "Recalculating index for npm repository <repoKey> scheduled to run", says it was queued, not that it finished. Needs the Manage permission on the repository. Only npm local repositories are reindexed; any other repository, npm remote and virtual ones included, is rejected with 400.

contract: Runs an AQL query. The body is the query text, not JSON, and is limited to 6,000 characters; longer bodies are rejected with 400 `AQL query is too long; please reduce the query length to less than 6000 chars`. A query has the form domain.find(criteria).include(fields).sort({"$asc"|"$desc":[fields]}).offset(n).limit(n), and may add .transitive() (accepted and ignored) and .distinct(bool) (default true). The suffixes may appear in any order, each at most once. Domains are items, properties, builds, build.promotions and the dotted secondary domains reachable from them; the archive.entries, item.infos, releases and release_artifacts domains are rejected with 400. Criteria are JSON objects, and several objects separated by commas are an implicit $and: {"field":value} means $eq; {"field":{"$op":value}} with $eq, $ne, $gt, $gte, $lt, $lte, $match, $nmatch, $before and $last; $and and $or combine them and siblings are an implicit $and; {"@key":value} and {"@*":value} address properties; {"$msp":[...]} matches on a single property. $before and $last take a number and a unit: ms, mills or millis; s or seconds; minutes or mi; d or days; w or weeks; mo or months; y or years. Wildcards * and ? apply only with $match and $nmatch and are matched case-sensitively. Every repository that stores items has a root, a folder whose path and name are ".", which an items query returns when its criteria match it. An include may name fields of the domains a relation path reaches, such as artifact.module.build.name, artifact.module.build.* or artifact: each found record then nests the related rows that meet the criteria under artifacts, dependencies, modules, builds, build.promotions or items, rows of one domain told apart by the fields included. An include may also name the properties of a related item, module or build (<path>.@key, <path>.@*, <path>.property.*) and the statistics of a related item (<path>.stat.*), and a builds query the properties of its own builds (@key, @*, property.*): they nest under properties (key, value), module.properties (module.property.key, module.property.value), build.properties (build.property.key, build.property.value) and stats of the row they belong to. An @key include returns only records whose related row has that key, and nests only such rows. An items query includes every property of each item with property, property.*, @ or @*, and one key with @key, which also returns only items that have it; @ and @* include every key wherever @key is accepted, and filter nothing. sort names only fields in the output. sort, offset and limit apply to the result rows, one per found record whatever the include: the properties, statistics and related rows of an item are listed inside its row, so offset(n) skips n items and limit(n) returns at most n items, each with all of its properties. An empty query is rejected with 400. An authenticated user is required, and anonymous callers are refused with 403; a user without admin rights may query the items domain, must include repo, path and name, and receives only rows they may read that the include and exclude patterns of the repository accept. With a token scoped build:<repository>/<path>:r such a user may also query builds and build.promotions; a builds query must include name, number and repo, and returns only the runs they may read. Nested rows, with their properties and statistics, are likewise only those such a user may read. For such a user, a scan-factor header above 1 (by default the configured non-admin scan factor) multiplies the rows a limited query reads before that filtering, so the limit can still be met. Every query returns at most the configured result cap (500,000 by default), its own limit included, and a trimmed result says so in range.notification. A query whose reads outlast the configured timeout (900 seconds by default, or 7,200 seconds with a stream: true header) is cancelled and answered with 408. The response is indented unless compact=true is in the query string. The actions items.delete(criteria).dryRun("true"|"false") and properties.update(criteria).keys(key,...).newValue(value).dryRun(...) change what their criteria select and answer in the same shape, listing the rows they change, or would change on a dry run. An action without dryRun is a dry run, and takes no include, sort, offset or limit. properties.update names item fields as item.<field> and replaces the values of the keys an item already has. A user without admin rights changes only rows they may read and also delete, or annotate; other rows are left out.

contract: Starts converting a local npm repository to strict layout. Every npm local repository here already behaves as one with "Enforce strict layout" on, so the conversion only moves tarballs: each .tgz that is stored but not indexed because it sits off its canonical path is moved to the canonical path its package.json gives, with its properties, and indexed there. A tarball without a readable package.json is left where it is, and so is one whose canonical path already holds the same content, which needs no move. A tarball whose canonical path holds anything else, or whose move the repository refuses, as its release and snapshot handling may, is left where it is too, and the conversion fails naming it, after moving every other tarball; the queue retries a failed conversion and parks it once its retries run out, for resume to queue again. The conversion is queued on the persistent work queue under the repository's key and runs in the background: asking again while one is pending joins it, and running it again after it finished changes nothing. Needs the Manage permission on the repository. Only npm local repositories convert; any other repository is rejected with 400. Answers 202 with no body.

contract: Stores the request body at the path. Needs deploy permission; the target must be a local repository or a virtual repository with a default deployment repository, otherwise 405. A path ending in `/` with an empty body creates a folder. Matrix parameters `;key=value` on the last path segment become properties. Checksums declared in `X-Checksum-*` headers are recorded as original checksums and verified against the stored bytes; a mismatch is rejected with 409. Responds 201 with the created item and its URL in `Location`, at the path it was stored at: in a local Maven, Gradle, Ivy or SBT repository with the `maven-2-default` layout, a snapshot file is renamed as the repository's `snapshotVersionBehavior` says, so `unique` stores `app-1.0-SNAPSHOT.jar` as `app-1.0-<yyyyMMdd.HHmmss>-<buildNumber>.jar`. Deploying over an existing path replaces the content unless the repository forbids overwrites; replacing needs delete permission at the stored path, except with the file's own content: a deploy that declares the stored file's SHA-1 or SHA-256 and stores those same bytes needs deploy permission only, and so does such a checksum deploy unless the server is set to require delete permission for it. A replacement refused for want of delete permission answers 403, or 401 to an anonymous caller, with the message `Not enough permissions to delete/overwrite artifact '<repoKey>:<path>' (user: '<user>' needs DELETE permission).`, naming the repository the file is in, its stored path (for an archive, the entry in the way) and the caller, `anonymous` for an anonymous one. A `.md5`, `.sha1`, `.sha256` or `.sha512` body for an existing file, or for any file in a Maven-family repository, records that checksum on the file and answers 201 with no body and the file's URL in `Location`. The same route carries two variants selected by headers. With `X-Explode-Archive: true` the body is a zip, tar, tar.gz or tgz archive whose entries are deployed under the target folder instead of the archive itself (`X-Explode-Archive-Atomic: true` makes the extraction all-or-nothing), answering 201 `text/plain` with no body. With `X-Checksum-Deploy: true` and a checksum header the server deploys an existing binary with that checksum without a body, answering 201. The caller must be able to read a file with that checksum, or send in `X-Checksum-Deploy-Token` the `checksumToken` of its own finished multipart upload of that content; otherwise, as when no binary matches, it answers 404 so the client uploads normally.
